name: Malignant Non-Dysgerminomatous Germ Cell Tumor of Ovary
aliases: Malignant Non-Dysgerminomatous Ovarian Germ Cell Tumor

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Female Genital Tumors

criteria.description: Histopathological confirmation of malignant non-dysgerminomatous germ cell tumor components (e.g., yolk sac tumor, embryonal carcinoma, choriocarcinoma, immature teratoma)
Elevated serum tumor markers such as alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG), or lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) consistent with non-dysgerminomatous germ cell tumor
Pelvic imaging (ultrasound, MRI, or CT) demonstrating ovarian mass with features suspicious for malignant germ cell tumor

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of malignant non-dysgerminomatous germ cell tumor with supportive elevated serum tumor markers
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of pure dysgerminoma and other ovarian malignancies.

pathognomonic.notes: Indicative of yolk sac tumor components
Suggests presence of choriocarcinoma or embryonal carcinoma elements

searchTerms: pain in lower abdomen or pelvis

common.notes: Due to tumor mass effect or ascites

common.symptomName: Constitutional symptoms such as weight loss
searchTerms: general symptoms like weight loss and fatigue
unexplained weight loss and feeling unwell

occasional.notes: May occur due to tumor invasion
searchTerms: vaginal bleeding not related to periods

occasional.notes: Secondary to mass effect or paraneoplastic phenomena
Due to tumor compression on adjacent organs

rare.notes: Due to rapid tumor growth causing adnexal twisting

imaging: Ultrasound showing complex adnexal mass with solid and cystic components
MRI demonstrating heterogeneous ovarian tumor with hemorrhagic or necrotic areas
CT scan for staging and detection of metastases
genetic: No specific germline mutations identified; somatic alterations may be present in tumor tissue
other: Histopathology revealing mixed malignant germ cell tumor components excluding pure dysgerminoma

distinguishingFeatures: Pure dysgerminoma histology without elevated AFP
Typically elevated LDH but normal AFP and β-hCG
Occurs in older women typically >40 years
Elevated CA-125 rather than AFP or β-hCG
Histology shows epithelial origin rather than germ cell

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging pelvic mass with severe abdominal pain
Markedly elevated AFP or β-hCG levels
Signs of ovarian torsion or acute abdomen
references: WHO Classification of Female Genital Tumors, 5th Edition, 2020
NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Ovarian Cancer, Version 3.2024
